learning_outcomes.text: Acquisition of knowledge regarding the calculation of combined stresses, the calculation of statically indeterminate systems, as well as the calculation for buckling and dynamic stresses due to shock and fatigue.
Familiarization with the types of combined stresses encountered in mechanical engineering.
Students' acquisition of the knowledge necessary for performing strength and deformability calculations of parts and structural elements, in static and dynamic regimes.
Acquisition of the mechanical behavior of structural elements/structures used in mechanical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Calculation of curved bars: Stresses and deformations in curved bar sections
Buckling of straight bars: Elastic stability
Dynamic stresses: Stresses due to inertia forces
Calculation for variable stresses: Material fatigue
Limit cycle diagrams and their schematizations
Strength calculation for combined stresses: oblique bending
Calculation of deformations: Calculation of deflections and rotations
Calculation of stresses and deformations of curved bars
Calculation of variable stresses: Strength calculation in case of shocks
Calculation of safety factor for fatigue
Occupational health and safety and fire protection norms + Laboratory presentation
Experimental determination of critical buckling force
Experimental determination of deformations in oblique bending
Measurement of deformations by resistive electrical tensometry
Determination of the theoretical stress concentration factor by photoelasticimetry
Impact test: Determination of fracture energy
Redoing lab work and concluding activities
assessment_rules: The final grade is based on a written exam (65%), seminar activities (30%), and a laboratory written test (5%). The written exam consists of 5 subjects (2 theory, 3 problems). Minimum performance standards include identifying combined stress types, acquiring fundamental notions, defining main mechanical stress types, and performing strength calculations for various combined stresses.
